cards.intuition: Serving path hot, recent work warm, archives cold. Each step down cuts the price by an order of magnitude and raises restore time.
cards.formula: hot = indexes + current chunks, cold = old generations
cards.topic: Hot vs Cold Storage Tiering for Corpora and Indexes

cards.intuition: Archive pricing hides retrieval fees and restore latency, so tier decisions test how fast you can get data back, not just what storage costs.
cards.formula: tier test = price + retrieval fee + restore latency
cards.topic: Hot vs Cold Storage Tiering for Corpora and Indexes

cards.intuition: Generations stay hot only for their rollback window, then go cold, then get deleted. Hot storage is never the default graveyard.
cards.formula: hot -> cold -> delete, on the rollback window
cards.topic: Hot vs Cold Storage Tiering for Corpora and Indexes

cards.intuition: Do inputs change per request, is the value space sparse, is the value reused, is the read latency budget tight. The answers pick write-time or read-time compute.
cards.topic: Precompute vs Compute-on-Read: The Decision Framework

cards.intuition: Precompute costs write compute plus storage plus invalidation upkeep; on-read costs reads times per-read compute. Compare them with real numbers.
cards.formula: write + store + invalidate vs reads x per-read cost
cards.topic: Precompute vs Compute-on-Read: The Decision Framework

cards.intuition: Precomputing values whose inputs churn buys invalidation storms and stale outputs; on-read pays per query for what one batch job could buy.
cards.formula: churning inputs + precompute = stale or storm
cards.topic: Precompute vs Compute-on-Read: The Decision Framework

cards.intuition: Let the compressed index recall candidates and full-precision vectors rescore only the top few hundred; recall loss drops to noise at a few percent extra compute.
cards.formula: compressed recall + full-precision rescore of top-k
cards.topic: Quantization and Index Compression: Recall per Dollar

cards.intuition: Measure recall at each compression level, price the memory of each, and pick the cheapest configuration above the recall floor.
cards.formula: plot recall@k vs memory cost, pick the knee
cards.topic: Quantization and Index Compression: Recall per Dollar

cards.intuition: Serving memory drives fleet size, so halving the vector working set can halve the fleet; compression is a finance decision made with retrieval metrics.
cards.topic: Quantization and Index Compression: Recall per Dollar

cards.intuition: Re-embed on a golden-set gain, measured drift, corpus shape change, or generation hygiene. Never on the calendar or a benchmark headline.
cards.formula: re-embed on evidence, not on dates
cards.topic: Re-embedding Cadence: When Quality Gains Justify Rebuilds

cards.intuition: Quality gain times traffic times value per better answer, minus rebuild cost and risk. If the gain cannot pay back, decline politely.
cards.formula: value = gain x traffic x worth - cost - risk
cards.topic: Re-embedding Cadence: When Quality Gains Justify Rebuilds

cards.intuition: New documents embed on the new model immediately, the chunks serving most traffic backfill first, and the alias swaps only after the gates pass.
cards.formula: new traffic now, hottest chunks first, swap last
cards.topic: Re-embedding Cadence: When Quality Gains Justify Rebuilds
